title: The Lingering Shadow of Rodrigo Duterte’s Drug War in the Philippines
gist: A reportage piece on the lasting human toll of police killings in Manila, centered on Salvacion Ramos, whose daughter Cristeta was shot by four plainclothes police officers on her doorstep in Batasan in February 2017. Ramos and fellow bereaved mother Llore Pasco remain in weekly contact and continue to seek justice.

insights.claim: In February 2017, Cristeta Ramos was shot once in the back and three times in the head by four plainclothes police officers on the doorstep of her mother's home in Batasan, on the outskirts of Manila.
insights.so_what: Individual cases like this form the evidentiary backbone of accountability efforts against Duterte-era police operations.
insights.quote: Cristeta Ramos was shot once in the back and three times in the head by four plainclothes police officers
insights.locator: It was on that same doorstep
insights.speaker: Aubin Eymard

insights.claim: Bereaved mothers Salvacion Ramos and Llore Pasco have stayed in close weekly contact since the deaths of their respective children and are fighting for justice.
insights.so_what: Sustained victim-family organizing keeps police killings a live political and legal accountability issue years after the fact.
insights.speaker: Aubin Eymard

insights.claim: At 68, Salvacion Ramos runs a small convenience store from her Manila-area home to pay for the education of the grandson she has raised since her daughter was killed by police.
insights.so_what: The legacy of police killings includes lasting household-level economic hardship for poor urban families, not just legal and political fallout.
insights.speaker: Aubin Eymard
